llm.summary: This skill is a local, consent-based learning log with no executable code or network behavior, though its broad trigger phrases could occasionally activate unexpectedly.

dimensions.detail: The artifact purpose is coherent: it records lessons, errors, best practices, reviews, and improvement suggestions into a local `.learnings/` directory, with repeated instructions for confirmation and sanitization before writes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Several natural-language triggers such as "记下来", "怎么改进", and "打个分" are broad enough to match ordinary conversation, but the skill discloses the behavior and requires confirmation before storing or clearing data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only Markdown, license, and changelog files; static scan found no suspicious patterns, no executable scripts are present, and the skill declares no required bins or environment variables.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: File access is scoped to reading and writing `.learnings/` files in the current project, which fits the stated self-improvement purpose. There is no artifact-backed evidence of uploads, cross-session access, hooks, or system-file modification.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill intentionally creates persistent local records and includes a disclosed clear-records action requiring double confirmation; this is expected for the purpose and not hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This is reasonable to install if you want a local project learning log. Use explicit requests when invoking it, review the proposed entry before confirming, and avoid confirming entries that include sensitive project details even though the skill instructs the agent to mask secrets.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: README trigger phrases are broad, so accidental activation is plausible, but the artifact limits impact through local-only storage, content preview, and required user confirmation before writes.
[SQP-1] expected: SKILL.md uses similarly broad trigger phrases; this is a usability and consent-scoping note rather than a policy concern because no automatic hooks, hidden execution, or unconfirmed storage are present.
